_comment: Permissions for the EC2 instance profile attached to the magik-prod box.
Attach ALONGSIDE the AWS-managed AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore (required for
cd.yml's SSM-based deploy to reach the box at all).
This file was previously undocumented: the box has relied on
ssm:GetParameter for /magik/ghcr_pat since Phase 30 (see cd.yml's
remote-deploy.sh, which runs ON this instance via SSM and calls
`aws ssm get-parameter --name /magik/ghcr_pat`), but the instance profile's
own policy was never captured as a repo file the way the two Lambda
policies were. Phase 31 (project memory 'secrets-management-gap') adds five
more app secrets to the same pattern and is the occasion to fix that gap.
A later pass (same memory doc, 2026-08-01) added four more --
qdrant_api_key, redis_token, hf_token, tavily_api_key -- after auditing
.env.example against what was actually still SSM-eligible. Note what is
deliberately NOT here: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID (OAuth client IDs are public by
design, only _SECRET is confidential) belongs in the committed
deploy/aws/prod.env instead, and grafana_admin_password / ntfy_webhook_url
are real secrets too but are consumed by the separately-deployed
monitoring stack, not this app container -- they get their own
statement below (ReadMonitoringSecretsAtDeployTime), same role, since
deploy/aws/scripts/deploy_monitoring.sh runs ON this same box under
this same instance profile, just fetching for a different docker
compose invocation.
Every Resource below is scoped to one exact parameter path -- this role
must not be able to read any other secret in Parameter Store, and must
never be granted a wildcard ssm:GetParameter.
